name: MercadoLibre
thesis: MercadoLibre is the Amazon + PayPal of Latin America — 18 countries, 220M+ active users, and a fintech arm (Mercado Pago) that is now bigger by revenue than the marketplace. Its logistics network (Mercado Envios) mirrors Amazon's FBA, creating a flywheel competitors cannot easily replicate. Revenue growing 40%+ YoY. ROIC improving as scale benefits kick in. Latin America fintech penetration still early innings.
keyRisks: Brazil FX weakness; regulatory risk in fintech (Banco Central do Brasil scrutiny); Amazon LatAm expansion; credit losses in Mercado Credito if macro deteriorates.
catalysts: Mercado Credito loan book growth; Mercado Pago offline payments (POS devices); Chile/Colombia expansion; ROIC expansion as logistics fixed costs are leveraged.

name: Palantir Technologies
thesis: Palantir built the most sophisticated data integration and AI deployment platform in existence, refined over 20 years of classified government work. Its AIP (Artificial Intelligence Platform) lets enterprises run AI on their own data with governance — something no cloud provider offers. US commercial revenue accelerating (55%+ growth). Government contracts (US Army, NHS, NATO allies) are decade-long relationships. Alex Karp is a visionary but controversial CEO.
keyRisks: Expensive valuation (100x+ earnings); government contract concentration; Alex Karp erratic communication; competition from Databricks, Snowflake, Palantir building on top of cloud hyperscalers.
catalysts: AIP Boot Camp commercial deal closings; US Defence budget expansion; NATO AI adoption post-Ukraine; FedRAMP authorised AI platform for civilian agencies; S&P 500 inclusion (achieved 2024).

name: Spotify
thesis: Spotify has 260M+ paid subscribers — 3x Apple Music — and the global audio network effects are irreversible. It is finally achieving operating leverage after years of music label costs. Gross margins expanding from 25% toward 30%+ as podcasts, audiobooks, and AI-personalised playlists generate higher-margin revenue. Daniel Ek is a visionary founder. The Creator Marketplace and Spotify for Podcasters are early-stage monetisation levers.
keyRisks: Apple/Google fee pressure on iOS/Android subscriptions; music label contract renewals (Universal, Warner, Sony have significant leverage); profitability still thin; podcast investments unproven ROI.
catalysts: Gross margin expansion to 35%+ over 3 years; audiobook subscriber conversion; AI DJ / personalised radio monetisation; video podcasts capturing YouTube share; emerging market subscriber growth.

name: Fair Isaac (FICO)
thesis: FICO is a legal monopoly on credit scoring in the US — virtually every mortgage, auto loan, and credit card uses a FICO score. Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac require it. Despite VantageScore (created by the three bureaus) as an alternative, FICO raised prices dramatically (2022-2024) and nobody left. Revenue per score is still tiny vs the K+ lending decision it informs. Software business (FICO Platform) growing 20%+ and not yet appreciated.
keyRisks: CFPB or Congressional scrutiny of FICO monopoly pricing; Fannie/Freddie allowing VantageScore; mortgage market slowdown reducing score volumes.
catalysts: FICO Platform (AI decisioning SaaS) reaching scale; continued B2B2C price increases; international credit scoring expansion (India, Latin America); buyback programme (repurchased 50%+ of shares in 10 years).

name: Constellation Software
thesis: Constellation is the greatest capital allocator in software — it acquires hundreds of vertical market software (VMS) businesses at 3-5x EBITDA, runs them permanently, and lets acquired teams retain autonomy. Mark Leonard (founder) has compounded book value at 35%+ for 20 years. The model is Berkshire Hathaway for software. Spinoffs (Topicus, Lumine) unlock further value.
keyRisks: Mark Leonard succession (he is the key architect); deal sizes must grow as CSU gets larger, compressing returns; limited liquidity of TSX-listed stock for US investors.
catalysts: Topicus.com European expansion; Lumine Group (telecoms VMS) global rollout; larger deals (>B) if multiples stay reasonable; international VMS markets (India, Brazil) opening.

name: Axon Enterprise
thesis: Axon is the de facto monopoly in law enforcement technology — Taser weapons (95%+ market share), body cameras (75%+ market share), and now a SaaS platform (Evidence.com) that stores and manages all law enforcement digital evidence. Recurring revenue growing 30%+. International expansion to UK, Australia, and EU just beginning. AI tools (Draft One — auto-generating police reports) are early but highly sticky.
keyRisks: Government budget constraints reducing law enforcement tech spend; legal/political backlash on Taser use of force; international regulatory hurdles; competition from Motorola Solutions.
catalysts: AI Draft One (report writing) expansion; Fleet (in-car cameras) cross-sell; international body camera wins; TASER 10 upgrade cycle; potential correction agency / military adjacency.

name: Copart
thesis: Copart runs the dominant global network of salvage vehicle auctions — 200+ locations, 4M vehicles processed per year, 750K+ registered buyers in 170 countries. It is a marketplace with extraordinary network effects: more sellers attract more buyers, which drives better prices, which attracts more sellers. Land ownership (750+ acres per facility) is a hard-to-replicate moat. Founder-influenced culture. Revenue growing 12-15% with 45%+ operating margins.
keyRisks: Autonomous vehicles reducing accident frequency; insurance companies internalising salvage (State Farm started its own); extreme weather events could spike claim volumes either way.
catalysts: International expansion (Germany, Middle East); EV salvage — Copart developing EV-specific auction lanes; virtual vehicle listings growth; total loss rate staying elevated as vehicle repair costs rise.

name: Nu Holdings (Nubank)
thesis: Nubank is the largest digital bank in Latin America — 100M+ customers across Brazil, Mexico, Colombia. Built entirely mobile-first with zero branches, giving it a structural cost advantage vs incumbent banks. Average revenue per user still very low (Mexico and Colombia just started monetising) while customer acquisition costs are near zero (word-of-mouth). Warren Buffett's Berkshire invested in 2021. David Vélez (founder) is exceptional.
keyRisks: Brazil macro deterioration and credit losses; regulatory risk (Banco Central); competition from Banco Inter, C6 Bank, PicPay; FX exposure (BRL/MXN vs USD).
catalysts: Mexico monetisation ramp (20M customers with very low ARPU); Colombia launch; NuBank insurance and investment products (NuInvest); potential expansion to US Hispanic market.

name: Heico Corporation
thesis: HEICO is the world's largest independent supplier of FAA-approved aircraft spare parts at 30-50% below OEM prices. Airlines have no choice but to buy expensive OEM parts or approved alternatives — HEICO sits in that sweet spot. The Mendelsohn family has compounded the business for 30+ years at 20%+ ROIC through disciplined bolt-on acquisitions. Aerospace aftermarket grows with every flight hour flown globally.
keyRisks: Boeing/Airbus OEMs fighting back with aggressive pricing; PMA (Parts Manufacturer Approval) parts adoption stalling; defence budget cuts in Electronic Technologies division.
catalysts: Post-COVID air travel recovery driving flight hours; Heico's acquisition pipeline (M+ per year); defence electronics growing; expanding into new FAA-approved parts categories.
